pages.what: Risk and hardship allowance. There are several rate classes, and the order names the class you are placed in.
pages.when: When you are posted to a station that qualifies and your unit is listed for it.
pages.ready: The date it starts, the station code, and the corps notification number and date together with the serial at which your unit is listed.
pages.watch: The class printed must be the one your unit is listed under. The order carries a certificate that you are stationed there and your unit is in the notification.

pages.what: The order that stops risk and hardship allowance from a date, for a station.
pages.when: When the allowance ends from a given date for a station.
pages.ready: The date it stops and the station code.
pages.watch: The stop date and station code should match the start entry you received earlier.

pages.what: Transport allowance, which has five categories: lower or higher rate by city, the same with a disability, and one for Major General and above.
pages.when: When you become entitled to transport allowance at a station.
pages.ready: The date it starts, the reason for the grant, the station, and for some categories the disability or the rank.
pages.watch: Choose the category by the manual's list. Allowance is for officers not given government transport for travel between home and duty.

pages.what: House rent allowance, in three versions that depend on the class of the city.
pages.when: When you become entitled to house rent allowance for a station.
pages.ready: The first and last day, the station, whether you are single or married, and whether this is the first or a later claim on the current posting.
pages.watch: It must be stopped when you are given accommodation or posted out. A stop entry exists for this.

pages.what: The start of ration money allowance, paid instead of free rations while you are away from your station in certain situations.
pages.when: When you are on leave, joining time, a course or similar, and ration cannot be drawn in kind.
pages.ready: The date it starts, what kind of leave or reason applies, and proof you drew no free ration or daily allowance for the period.
pages.watch: It is always followed by a stop entry. For long absences, such as maternity or study leave, orders are published quarterly in arrears to avoid overpayment.

pages.what: The date you were struck off the ration strength of your unit.
pages.when: Whenever your ration status changes.
pages.ready: The date from which it applies.
pages.watch: The order carries only a date, so check it against your leave or posting dates.

pages.what: The date you were taken back on the ration strength of your unit.
pages.when: Whenever your ration status changes.
pages.ready: The date from which it applies.
pages.watch: The order carries only a date, so check it against your leave or posting dates.

pages.what: The date you assumed a named appointment.
pages.when: When you take over an appointment.
pages.ready: The date and the name of the appointment.
pages.watch: Only the date and the appointment name are recorded; keep the name exactly as in the posting order.

pages.what: The date you gave up a named appointment.
pages.when: When you hand over an appointment.
pages.ready: The date and the name of the appointment.
pages.watch: Only the date and the appointment name are recorded; check both against your handover.

pages.what: Substantive promotion to a higher rank.
pages.when: Immediately on promotion. The option for pay fixation follows afterwards.
pages.ready: The new rank, the date, the service completed or sanction details, and the promotion sanction letter number and date.
pages.watch: The sanction letter number and date are quoted as authority. The pay fixation option order and certificate come after this entry.

pages.what: The order that records annual leave you were granted for one calendar year, with its first and last day.
pages.when: Whenever annual leave is granted. If you take leave for two years back to back, you see two separate entries, one per year.
pages.ready: First and last day of the leave, number of days, the leave year, and any weekend or holiday joined before (prefix) or after (suffix) the leave.
pages.watch: The number of days must match the dates exactly. An order that counts the days wrongly can be rejected in audit.

pages.what: Annual leave of an earlier year that was carried forward and is now being taken, for example after a UN Mission posting.
pages.when: When you take annual leave that was carried forward from a previous year.
pages.ready: First and last day, number of days, the leave year it belongs to, and the number and date of the order that allowed the carry forward.
pages.watch: The authority for carrying the leave forward has to be named in the order.

pages.what: Casual leave granted for a year, with its first and last day.
pages.when: Whenever casual leave is granted.
pages.ready: First and last day, number of days, the year, and any weekend or holiday added after the leave.
pages.watch: Casual leave cannot be joined with any other kind of leave, except special casual leave.

pages.what: Furlough leave, granted for one three-year cycle.
pages.when: When furlough leave is granted. If it comes with annual leave, the annual leave entry comes first.
pages.ready: First and last day, number of days, and the cycle, for example the years it covers. Any prefix or suffix days are given separately.
pages.watch: Furlough is granted only inside its own cycle. It is not given for an earlier cycle or as a continuation of one, and not to NCC or re-employed officers.

pages.what: Terminal leave, the leave granted as you come to the end of your service.
pages.when: When terminal leave is granted.
pages.ready: First and last day and the number of days. Prefix and suffix days are kept out of those dates.
pages.watch: If terminal leave is joined with annual leave, both entries are published together, and the yearly increment and most allowances do not run during that joined period.

pages.what: The yearly record of annual leave you have accumulated, with encashment taken on leave travel concession.
pages.when: Once a year, on or after the first of March of the following year, or on retirement.
pages.ready: The date as of which the total is stated, leave added for the year, the total at your credit, the earlier balance, and leave encashed on travel concession.
pages.watch: Leave added for one year should not pass thirty days, and the total at your credit must match what you have actually accumulated.

pages.what: Advance payment for encashing annual leave when you are going on leave travel concession.
pages.when: When you apply, sixty days or less before the planned journey.
pages.ready: The planned outward date, how much leave is at your credit, and how many days you want to encash.
pages.watch: If the journey is cancelled you must refund the advance within one month, or it is recovered from your salary. The same applies if the claim is rejected.

pages.what: Encashment of annual leave for leave travel concession after the journey is completed.
pages.when: When you have completed the journey.
pages.ready: The date as of which the totals are shown, the journey dates, the days at your credit, the days you are encashing and the total encashed so far in your career.
pages.watch: Encashment is allowed only when you are entitled to claim the travel concession, and it is taken from leave already accumulated.

pages.what: Children's education allowance for a child, with versions for a twin child and a divyang child.
pages.when: Every time you claim it.
pages.ready: The child's name, date of birth and standard, the period claimed, and the total amount claimed.
pages.watch: It is for the first two children, or a third only if twins were born second. There is an upper age limit and an order is needed for every claim.

pages.what: Hostel subsidy for a child, with versions for a twin child and a divyang child.
pages.when: Every time you claim it.
pages.ready: The child's name, date of birth and standard, the period claimed, and a certificate from the head of the school.
pages.watch: The same child limits apply as for children's education allowance, and both can be claimed together. A new order is needed for each claim.

pages.what: Your marriage, with details of your spouse.
pages.when: After you marry.
pages.ready: The date of marriage, your spouse's date of birth, name of your spouse's parents, nationality, and proof of the spouse's date of birth.
pages.watch: Proof of the spouse's date of birth is needed, from a list in the manual. If your spouse is in service or in government employ, a second entry follows.

pages.what: The birth of your child.
pages.when: After a child is born.
pages.ready: The child's name, date of birth, and whether a son or daughter.
pages.watch: Only the child's name, son or daughter, and date of birth are recorded.

pages.what: Proceeding to a course that lasts less than ten weeks.
pages.when: When you leave for such a course.
pages.ready: The course name and station, dates, and details of any leave taken with the course.
pages.watch: It is for short courses only. A separate entry records the day you rejoin.

pages.what: The entry that records you were taken on strength of a new unit when posted in.
pages.when: On every posting to a unit.
pages.ready: The date, the unit number (SUS number), the station, the name of the unit, and whether the station is peace, field or another area type.
pages.watch: The date you joined the new unit should be the same as the date you left the previous one. The posting letter from the Army headquarters is quoted as authority.

pages.what: The entry that records you were struck off strength of a unit when posted out.
pages.when: On every posting out of a unit.
pages.ready: The date, the unit number (SUS number), the station, the name of the new unit, and the type of area.
pages.watch: Allowances tied to the old location, appointment or unit are ended through this entry.

pages.what: Your declaration of a selected place of residence when posted to a field, operational, hard or similar area.
pages.when: Within four months of the posting, which can be extended by two months with the station commander's permission.
pages.ready: The date, the name of the place you select, and the type of area you are posted to.
pages.watch: Missing the time limit can cost you house rent allowance and baggage, car and family move claims for that posting. It cannot be your own place of posting.

pages.what: Joining time granted when you are posted to a new unit.
pages.when: When you are posted to a unit and granted joining time.
pages.ready: First and last day of the joining time.
pages.watch: It is not granted on first posting after commissioning. If joined with other leave, joining time is taken last, and above thirty days a sanction letter is needed.

pages.what: The order for a temporary duty, from the day you leave to the day you rejoin.
pages.when: Whenever you go on temporary duty and when you rejoin.
pages.ready: The day you left, the day you rejoined, the station, and whether daily allowance is claimed or not.
pages.watch: Say clearly whether daily allowance was claimed, because the order records that choice.

pages.what: The order that cancels a whole earlier Part II order.
pages.when: When every entry of an earlier order has to be cancelled.
pages.ready: The number and date of the order being cancelled.
pages.watch: Where the entries are more than two years old, a time bar sanction is enclosed. The order also states that the earlier status is restored.

pages.what: The order that cancels one entry of an earlier Part II order.
pages.when: When just one entry of an earlier order was wrong or has to be withdrawn.
pages.ready: The order number and date, the serial number of the entry, and its occurrence code.
pages.watch: It cancels one entry only. If more than two years old, a time bar sanction is enclosed.
